title: Sounding natural
goal: React like a local, use tag questions and emphasis particles, make echo words, ask people to repeat or explain, get round words you don't know, and mix in English the way people in Pune and Mumbai do.
intro:
You can now say almost anything in Marathi. This unit is about saying it the way Marathi speakers do. Native speakers react all the time (**खरंच?**, **आईशप्पथ!**, **छे!**), tag their sentences (**…ना?**, **…नाही का?**, **…हं!**), and lean on tiny emphasis words (**-च**, **तर**, **की**). They also make echo words (**चहा-बिहा** 'tea or something') and drop English into nearly every sentence.

You'll also learn the survival skills every learner needs: asking someone to repeat or slow down, asking what a word means, filling a pause while you look for the word, and describing a thing when you don't know its name.

vocab.note: As a question, खरंच? = 'really?'. From खरं 'true' + emphatic -च.
For a sudden surprise or realisation: अरेच्चा, विसरलोच!

grammar.title: Tag questions: ना?, नाही का?, हो की नाही?, हं
grammar.body:
Marathi tags are short and used constantly — leaving them out makes you sound stiff.

**ना?** — the all-purpose 'right?', expecting yes: तू येणार आहेस **ना?** 'you're coming, right?' After a command it is a softener, not a question: सांग **ना** 'oh go on, tell me', ये **ना** 'do come'.

**हो ना?** — 'isn't that so?'; and as a reply, **हो ना!** 'I know, right!'

**नाही का?** — 'isn't it?', inviting the other person to agree: छान आहे, **नाही का?**

**हो की नाही?** — 'yes or no?', pushing for an answer: तू येतोयस, हो की नाही?

**बरोबर?** — 'correct?', when checking a fact.

**हं** at the end — 'OK? mind you', a friendly reminder or warning: उद्या वेळेवर ये **हं**!

**ना** in the middle is a filler meaning 'you know': तो **ना**, कधीच वेळेवर येत नाही 'him, you know, he's never on time'.

The trap: **का** and **ना** do different jobs. तू येणार आहेस **का**? is an open question ('are you coming?'); तू येणार आहेस **ना**? assumes yes ('you are coming, right?'). Don't stack them.

examples.en: Oh come on, tell me what happened.

grammar.title: Emphasis: -च, तर, की, -ही
grammar.body:
**-च** — joined to any word: 'only, the very, exactly, definitely'. **मीच** 'I myself / only I', **आजच** 'today itself', **हेच** 'this very thing', **तसंच** 'just like that', **नक्कीच** 'definitely'. Its position changes the meaning: **मीच** तिला सांगितलं 'it was *me* who told her'; मी **तिलाच** सांगितलं 'I told *her* (and no one else)'.

**तर** — 'as for, really, actually': मी **तर** नाही जाणार 'I, for one, am not going'; हे **तर** भन्नाट आहे 'this is just amazing'; ये **तर**! 'come on then!'

**की** at the end of a reply — 'of course!', contradicting a doubt: पार्किंग आहे का? — आहे **की**! 'Of course there is!'; with a command it urges: ये **की**! 'do come!'

**-ही / -सुद्धा / पण** — 'too, even': मला**ही**, मला**सुद्धा**, मला **पण** 'me too' (पण 'too' is very colloquial); कोणी**ही** 'anyone at all', कधी**ही** 'any time'.

**Intensifiers**: **अजिबात** + negative 'not at all'; **भलताच** 'awfully, unusually' (agrees: भलतीच हुशार); and the slang **जाम** and **लय** 'super, really' — friends only.

The trap: -च is spoken **ts** and written joined: मीच, not मी च.

examples.en: It was me who told her.
I told her and only her.

grammar.title: Echo words and doubled words: चहा-बिहा, हळूहळू
grammar.body:
**Echo words**: repeat a word, swapping its first consonant (or adding one) with **बि-**: चहा → **चहा-बिहा**, जेवण → **जेवण-बिवण**, पैसे → **पैसे-बिसे**, पार्टी → **पार्टी-बिर्टी**. It means 'X and that sort of thing, X or something': चहा-बिहा घेणार का? 'will you have tea or something?' It is casual and friendly, but can also be dismissive: अभ्यास-बिभ्यास काही नाही 'no studying or anything'. Endings go only on the end: चहा-बिहा**ला** या.

**Doubled words** do several jobs:
- gradually / manner: **हळूहळू** 'slowly, bit by bit', **गरमागरम** 'piping hot', **मध्ये मध्ये** 'every now and then; cutting in'
- frequency: **कधी कधी** 'sometimes'
- every, distributive: **घरोघरी** 'in every home', **एक एक** 'one by one'
- 'what all, who all' when you expect a list: **काय काय** केलंस? **कोण कोण** येणार आहे? **कुठे कुठे** गेलात?
- variety: **वेगवेगळा** 'various, different'

Using काय काय and कोण कोण instead of a plain काय / कोण is one of the quickest ways to sound like a native.

examples.en: Have some tea or something before you go.
I don't want money or anything.
Bit by bit I started getting the hang of Marathi.
At Diwali, lanterns go up in every home.

dialogue.title: Lay bhari!
dialogue.setting: Sam, who has been learning Marathi for a year, meets his Pune friends Omkar and Pooja at a tea stall on JM Road.

lines.en: Hey Sam, will you have some tea or something?

lines.speaker: Sam

lines.speaker: Omkar
lines.en: Get out of here! Who taught you that?

lines.en: The rickshaw drivers. They say it all day long, don't they?

lines.speaker: Pooja

lines.roman: ho nā! paṇ ek sāṅg, tulā marāṭhī avghaḍ nāhī vāṭat?
lines.en: They do! But tell me something — don't you find Marathi hard?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: अं… कधी कधी. तुम्ही लोक जाम फास्ट बोलता! आणि 'ळ' चा उच्चार तर…
lines.roman: aṃ… kadhī kadhī. tumhī lok dzām fāsṭ boltā! āṇi 'ḷ' tsā uchchār tar…
lines.en: Um… sometimes. You lot talk super fast! And as for pronouncing 'ḷ'…

lines.speaker: Omkar
lines.en: Don't stress. You'll get there bit by bit.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: मध्येच टोकल्याबद्दल सॉरी, पण 'जमेल' म्हणजे काय?
lines.roman: madhyets ṭoklyābaddal sôrī, paṇ 'dzamel' mhaṇje kāy?
lines.en: Sorry to interrupt, but what does 'jamel' mean?

lines.speaker: Pooja
lines.native: म्हणजे… तुला येईल. बेसिकली, तू करू शकशील!
lines.roman: mhaṇje… tulā yeīl. besikalī, tū karū shakshīl!
lines.en: It means… you'll get it. Basically, you'll be able to do it!

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: हां, कळलं! मग मी तर नक्कीच शिकणार.
lines.roman: hāṃ, kaḷlaṃ! mag mī tar nakkīts shikṇār.
lines.en: Ah, got it! Then I'm definitely going to learn it.

lines.speaker: Omkar
lines.en: Awesome! Come on, now a vada pav or something?

culture:
Marathi changes a lot from city to city. **Pune** Marathi is seen as the 'standard' (and Puneris are famous for being blunt and a little sarcastic); **Mumbai** Marathi is fast and mixed with Hindi and English ('Bambaiya'); **Kolhapur** gives the whole state **लय भारी**; **Nagpur** and Vidarbha sound different again, and the **Konkan** coast has its own soft lilt. Young people everywhere mix in English — ॲक्च्युअली, बेसिकली, सिरियसली, ओके, डन — always with Marathi verbs and tags around it.

Listening is active: say **हं**, **हो**, **बरं**, **खरंच?** while someone talks, or they'll think you've stopped listening. Young men often use mild expletives like **आयला** or **च्यायला** ('damn!') as reactions — fine among friends, not in front of elders. And a very common experience for learners: the moment people notice you're not a native speaker, they switch to Hindi or English to be helpful. Smile and say **मराठीत बोला ना, मला शिकायचं आहे** 'please speak Marathi, I want to learn' — people are usually delighted, and that one sentence opens a lot of doors.

tip.title: React, react, react
tip.body:
- Surprise: **खरंच?**, **हो का?**, **अरेच्चा!**, **आईशप्पथ!**
- Disbelief: **काय सांगतोस!**, **छे!**, **चल हट!** (friends only).
- Disgust: **शी!** Mothers and aunties say **अगंबाई!**
- React out loud — silence sounds cold in Marathi.

sentences.en: Really? I had no idea!
Well I never — what are you doing here? (to a man)
Oh my, look how big you've grown! (to a girl)
Nah, nothing like that happened.
I swear, I'm telling the truth! (man)
Ugh, it's so dirty here!
Her wedding's been fixed? Oh really?
You don't say! He's gone abroad?
Come off it, you're kidding.

tip.title: ना?, नाही का?, हं — tagging your sentences
tip.body:
- **ना?** 'right?' (expects yes): तू येणार आहेस **ना?**
- **नाही का?** 'isn't it?' — invites agreement.
- **हो की नाही?** 'yes or no?' — pushes for an answer.
- **हं** at the end: 'OK? mind you': लवकर ये **हं**!
- After a command, **ना** softens: सांग **ना**.

tip.title: -च, तर, की — adding punch
tip.body:
- **-च** 'the very / only / definitely': **मीच** करणार, **आजच**, **नक्कीच**.
- **तर** 'as for / really': मी **तर** नाही जाणार.
- **की** at the end: 'of course!': आहे **की**!
- Intensifiers: **अजिबात** (+ not), **भलताच** (agrees), and slangy **जाम**, **लय**.

sentences.en: I'll do this job myself.
I've got no time at all.

sentences.native: मी तर नाही जाणार, तू जा.
sentences.roman: mī tar nāhī dzāṇār, tū dzā.
sentences.en: Well, I'm not going — you go.
Is there parking? Of course there is!
It was super crowded today.
She's awfully clever.
Awesome!
That's exactly what I was saying! (man)
I want to come too.
Do come, everyone's waiting!

tip.title: चहा-बिहा, हळूहळू, काय काय
tip.body:
- Echo word: repeat with **बि-**: चहा-**बिहा**, जेवण-**बिवण** = 'X or something'.
- Endings go on the end: चहा-बिहा**ला** या.
- Doubled for 'gradually': **हळूहळू**.
- For lists: **काय काय**, **कोण कोण** 'what all, who all'.

sentences.en: Will you have some tea or something, or shall we go?
Have you eaten and all?
Don't bother about money or anything — just come.
It will all come together bit by bit.
What all did you do in the holidays?
Who's coming to the wedding?
In Mumbai you get to hear all sorts of languages.
Stop cutting in!

sentences.native: कधी कधी मला मराठी स्वप्नंसुद्धा पडतात!
sentences.roman: kadhī kadhī malā marāṭhī svapnaṃsuddhā paḍtāt!
sentences.en: Sometimes I even dream in Marathi!

tip.title: Asking people to repeat or explain
tip.body:
- Repeat: **पुन्हा एकदा सांगता का?** (polite) / **परत सांग ना** (friend).
- Slower: **जरा सावकाश बोला ना**.
- A word: **याचा अर्थ काय?**, **याला मराठीत काय म्हणतात?**
- Buying time: **अं…**, **काय म्हणतात ते…** — natives do it too.

sentences.en: Sorry, could you say that again? I didn't get it.

The sound 'ḷ' is hard to pronounce.

sentences.roman: yā don shabdāntsā artha ekts āhe kā?

lessons.title: Mixing in English and getting round words

tip.title: Mixing in English, describing what you can't name
tip.body:
- English fillers slot straight in: **ॲक्च्युअली**, **बेसिकली**, **सिरियसली**.
- English verbs need a Marathi helper: **मिक्स करणे**, **कॅन्सल होणे**.
- Don't know the word? Describe it: **एक प्रकारचा** गोड पदार्थ 'a kind of sweet dish'.
- Ask to be corrected: **मी चुकलो तर टोका**.
